questions.question: Why does a correct heading hierarchy (one h1, no skipped levels) matter for screen reader users specifically?
options: It doesn't affect screen readers at all, only visual styling
Screen reader users frequently navigate a page by jumping between headings, so a broken hierarchy makes that navigation confusing or misleading
Screen readers cannot read a page without an h1
It only matters for search engine rankings, not accessibility
questions.explanation: Jumping by heading level is a common screen-reader navigation pattern, so the heading structure needs to accurately reflect the page's real content outline.

questions.question: What does the viewport meta tag actually control?
options: The page's title shown in the browser tab
How mobile browsers size and scale the page — without it, mobile browsers render at a fixed desktop-like width and zoom out
The page's social media preview image
questions.explanation: Without a viewport meta tag, responsive CSS breakpoints don't work as intended on mobile, since the browser assumes a desktop viewport width by default.

questions.question: What are the `og:title`/`og:description`/`og:image` meta tags used for?
options: They control search engine ranking directly
Platforms like Twitter/X, Slack, and LinkedIn read them to build the preview card shown when a link is shared
They are required for the page to load at all
questions.explanation: Open Graph tags specifically target link-preview generation on social and messaging platforms, separate from standard search engine indexing.

questions.question: Why is a client-side-only rendered page potentially risky for SEO and link previews?
options: Client-side rendering is always slower, which is the only issue
Its initial HTML response is nearly empty, and not every crawler or social-preview bot executes JavaScript reliably or promptly to see the real content
Search engines refuse to index any JavaScript-based website
It has no actual impact on SEO
questions.explanation: Some crawlers do run JavaScript, but inconsistently; content present in the initial HTML response is the most reliably indexed and previewed, which is why server rendering/static generation is the safer default for SEO-sensitive content.
